name: RANDARRAY
description: RANDARRAY returns a dynamic array of random numbers, with a chosen number of rows and columns, bounds, and the option for whole numbers.
tldr: Generates an array of random numbers.

parameters.name: rows
parameters.description: The number of rows to return (defaults to 1).

parameters.name: columns
parameters.description: The number of columns to return (defaults to 1).

parameters.name: max
parameters.description: The largest value (inclusive for integers); defaults to 1.

parameters.name: integer
parameters.description: FALSE for decimal values (default) or TRUE for whole numbers.

basicExample.description: A 3-row by 2-column block of random decimals
basicExample.result: Six random decimals between 0 and 1 in a 3x2 array
basicExample.explanation: With no bounds supplied, RANDARRAY returns values from 0 to 1.

advancedExamples.title: Random integers in a range
advancedExamples.scenario: Five random whole numbers from 1 to 100.
advancedExamples.explanation: integer TRUE forces whole numbers within the 1-100 bounds.

advancedExamples.title: Decimal grid within bounds
advancedExamples.explanation: integer FALSE keeps the results as decimals.

howItWorks: RANDARRAY returns an array of random numbers. With no arguments it returns a single random decimal between 0 and 1. rows and columns set the size, min and max set the bounds, and integer forces whole numbers. Like RAND, it recalculates and produces new values on every change.

howToSteps.name: Set bounds and type
howToSteps.text: Optionally set min, max, and integer.

howToSteps.name: Ensure spill space
howToSteps.text: Leave empty cells for the array.

limitations: Volatile: recalculates on every change, which can slow large sheets.
min must be less than max; integer results are inclusive of the bounds.

commonErrors.fix: Ensure min is less than max.

commonErrors.cause: No room for the spilled array.
commonErrors.fix: Clear the cells in the spill range.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: RANDARRAY is available in newer versions of Google Sheets; older Sheets may lack it and would need ARRAYFORMULA(RAND()) as a workaround.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: In Sheets the signature and behavior match Excel for supported versions.

faq.question: Is RANDARRAY in Google Sheets?
faq.answer: Yes, in recent Google Sheets versions; older Sheets may not support it.

faq.question: How do I get integers?
faq.answer: Set the integer argument to TRUE.

faq.question: Why do the values keep changing?
faq.answer: Like RAND, RANDARRAY is volatile and recalculates on every change.
